1	# skills
2	
3	The CLI for the open agent skills ecosystem.
4	
5	<!-- agent-list:start -->
6	Supports **OpenCode**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **Cursor**, and [70 more](#supported-agents).
7	<!-- agent-list:end -->
8	
9	[![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/vercel-labs/skills)](https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/skills)
10	
11	## Install a Skill
12	
13	```bash
14	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills
15	```
16	
17	## Use a Skill Without Installing
18	
19	Generate a prompt for one skill, or start a supported coding agent interactively:
20	
21	```bash
22	npx skills use vercel-labs/agent-skills@web-design-guidelines | claude
23	npx skills use vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill web-design-guidelines --agent claude-code
24	```
25	
26	`skills use` resolves sources the same way as `skills add`, writes the selected skill files to a temporary directory, and prints only the generated prompt to stdout unless `--agent` is provided. With `--agent`, it starts one supported agent interactively with the generated prompt.
27	
28	### Source Formats
29	
30	```bash
31	# GitHub shorthand (owner/repo)
32	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills
33	
34	# Full GitHub URL
35	npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills
36	
37	# Direct path to a skill in a repo
38	npx skills add https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills/tree/main/skills/web-design-guidelines
39	
40	# GitLab URL
41	npx skills add https://gitlab.com/org/repo
42	
43	# Any git URL
44	npx skills add git@github.com:vercel-labs/agent-skills.git
45	
46	# Local path
47	npx skills add ./my-local-skills
48	```
49	
50	### Options
51	
52	| Option                    | Description                                                                                                                                        |
53	| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
54	| `-g, --global`            | Install to user directory instead of project                                                                                                       |
55	| `-a, --agent <agents...>` | <!-- agent-names:start -->Target specific agents (e.g., `claude-code`, `codex`). See [Supported Agents](#supported-agents)<!-- agent-names:end --> |
56	| `-s, --skill <skills...>` | Install specific skills by name (use `'*'` for all skills)                                                                                         |
57	| `-l, --list`              | List available skills without installing                                                                                                           |
58	| `--copy`                  | Copy files instead of symlinking to agent directories                                                                                              |
59	| `-y, --yes`               | Skip all confirmation prompts                                                                                                                      |
60	| `--all`                   | Install all skills to all agents without prompts                                                                                                   |
61	
62	### Examples
63	
64	```bash
65	# List skills in a repository
66	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --list
67	
68	# Install specific skills
69	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill frontend-design --skill skill-creator
70	
71	# Install a skill with spaces in the name (must be quoted)
72	npx skills add owner/repo --skill "Convex Best Practices"
73	
74	# Install to specific agents
75	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills -a claude-code -a opencode
76	
77	# Non-interactive installation (CI/CD friendly)
78	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill frontend-design -g -a claude-code -y
79	
80	# Install all skills from a repo to all agents
81	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --all
82	
83	# Install all skills to specific agents
84	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill '*' -a claude-code
85	
86	# Install specific skills to all agents
87	npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --agent '*' --skill frontend-design
88	```
89	
90	### Installation Scope
91	
92	| Scope       | Flag      | Location            | Use Case                                      |
93	| ----------- | --------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
94	| **Project** | (default) | `./<agent>/skills/` | Committed with your project, shared with team |
95	| **Global**  | `-g`      | `~/<agent>/skills/` | Available across all projects                 |
96	
97	### Installation Methods
98	
99	When installing interactively, you can choose:
100	
101	| Method                    | Description                                                                                 |
102	| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
103	| **Symlink** (Recommended) | Creates symlinks from each agent to a canonical copy. Single source of truth, easy updates. |
104	| **Copy**                  | Creates independent copies for each agent. Use when symlinks aren't supported.              |
105	
106	## Other Commands
107	
108	| Command                      | Description                                   |
109	| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
110	| `npx skills use <source>`    | Use one skill without installing              |
111	| `npx skills list`            | List installed skills (alias: `ls`)           |
112	| `npx skills find [query]`    | Search for skills interactively or by keyword |
113	| `npx skills remove [skills]` | Remove installed skills from agents           |
114	| `npx skills update [skills]` | Update installed skills to latest versions    |
115	| `npx skills init [name]`     | Create a new SKILL.md template                |
116	
117	### `skills list`
118	
119	List all installed skills. Similar to `npm ls`.
120	
121	```bash
122	# List all installed skills (project and global)
123	npx skills list
124	
125	# List only global skills
126	npx skills ls -g
127	
128	# Filter by specific agents
129	npx skills ls -a claude-code -a cursor
130	```
131	
132	### `skills find`
133	
134	Search for skills interactively or by keyword.
135	
136	```bash
137	# Interactive search (fzf-style)
138	npx skills find
139	
140	# Search by keyword
141	npx skills find typescript
142	
143	# Search across every repository owned by an organization or user
144	npx skills find react --owner vercel
145	```
146	
147	### `skills update`
148	
149	```bash
150	# Update all skills (interactive scope prompt)
151	npx skills update
152	
153	# Update a single skill by name
154	npx skills update my-skill
155	
156	# Update multiple specific skills
157	npx skills update frontend-design web-design-guidelines
158	
159	# Update only global or project skills
160	npx skills update -g
161	npx skills update -p
162	
163	# Non-interactive (auto-detects scope: project if in a project, else global)
164	npx skills update -y
165	```
166	
167	| Option          | Description                                                               |
168	| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
169	| `-g, --global`  | Only update global skills                                                 |
170	| `-p, --project` | Only update project skills                                                |
171	| `-y, --yes`     | Skip scope prompt (auto-detect: project if in a project dir, else global) |
172	| `[skills...]`   | Update specific skills by name instead of all                             |
173	
174	### `skills init`
175	
176	```bash
177	# Create SKILL.md in current directory
178	npx skills init
179	
180	# Create a new skill in a subdirectory
181	npx skills init my-skill
182	```
183	
184	### `skills remove`
185	
186	Remove installed skills from agents.
187	
188	```bash
189	# Remove interactively (select from installed skills)
190	npx skills remove
191	
192	# Remove specific skill by name
193	npx skills remove web-design-guidelines
194	
195	# Remove multiple skills
196	npx skills remove frontend-design web-design-guidelines
197	
198	# Remove from global scope
199	npx skills remove --global web-design-guidelines
200	
201	# Remove from specific agents only
202	npx skills remove --agent claude-code cursor my-skill
203	
204	# Remove all installed skills without confirmation
205	npx skills remove --all
206	
207	# Remove all skills from a specific agent
208	npx skills remove --skill '*' -a cursor
209	
210	# Remove a specific skill from all agents
211	npx skills remove my-skill --agent '*'
212	
213	# Use 'rm' alias
214	npx skills rm my-skill
215	```
216	
217	| Option         | Description                                      |
218	| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
219	| `-g, --global` | Remove from global scope (~/) instead of project |
220	| `-a, --agent`  | Remove from specific agents (use `'*'` for all)  |
221	| `-s, --skill`  | Specify skills to remove (use `'*'` for all)     |
222	| `-y, --yes`    | Skip confirmation prompts                        |
223	| `--all`        | Shorthand for `--skill '*' --agent '*' -y`       |
224	
225	## What are Agent Skills?
226	
227	Agent skills are reusable instruction sets that extend your coding agent's capabilities. They're defined in `SKILL.md`
228	files with YAML frontmatter containing a `name` and `description`.
229	
230	Skills let agents perform specialized tasks like:
231	
232	- Generating release notes from git history
233	- Creating PRs following your team's conventions
234	- Integrating with external tools (Linear, Notion, etc.)
235	
236	Discover skills at **[skills.sh](https://skills.sh)**
237	
238	## Supported Agents
239	
240	Skills can be installed to any of these agents:
241	
242	<!-- supported-agents:start -->

327	## Creating Skills
328	
329	Skills are directories containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter:
330	
331	```markdown
332	---
333	name: my-skill
334	description: What this skill does and when to use it
335	---
336	
337	# My Skill
338	
339	Instructions for the agent to follow when this skill is activated.
340	
341	## When to Use
342	
343	Describe the scenarios where this skill should be used.
344	
345	## Steps
346	
347	1. First, do this
348	2. Then, do that
349	```
350	
351	### Required Fields
352	
353	- `name`: Unique identifier (lowercase, hyphens allowed)
354	- `description`: Brief explanation of what the skill does
355	
356	### Optional Fields
357	
358	- `metadata.internal`: Set to `true` to hide the skill from normal discovery. Internal skills are only visible and
359	  installable when `INSTALL_INTERNAL_SKILLS=1` is set. Useful for work-in-progress skills or skills meant only for
360	  internal tooling.
361	
362	```markdown
363	---
364	name: my-internal-skill
365	description: An internal skill not shown by default
366	metadata:
367	  internal: true
368	---
369	```

373	The CLI searches for skills in these locations within a repository. Each
374	skill container directory is walked one level deep for the common flat
375	layout (`skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) and one extra level deep for catalog
376	layouts (`skills/<category>/<name>/SKILL.md`). A `SKILL.md` discovered at
377	the shallower level shadows anything nested below it. Use `--full-depth`
378	to also discover `SKILL.md` files outside these container directories
379	(e.g. under `examples/` or `tests/`).

444	If `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` or `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` exists, skills declared in those files are also discovered:

453	      "source": "my-plugin",

478	### "No skills found"

480	Ensure the repository contains valid `SKILL.md` files with both `name` and `description` in the frontmatter.

486	- Ensure the `SKILL.md` frontmatter is valid YAML
487

496	| `INSTALL_INTERNAL_SKILLS` | Set to `1` or `true` to show and install skills marked as `internal: true` |

502	INSTALL_INTERNAL_SKILLS=1 npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --list

24

26	
27	- `npx skills find [query] [--owner <owner>]` - Search for skills interactively or by keyword, optionally scoped to a GitHub owner

38

summary:
Based on my exploration of the vercel-labs/skills repository, here's a comprehensive analysis of how remote skills are resolved and the directory structure assumptions:

## Remote Skill Resolution Process ("skill add <remote>")

The resolution happens in multiple stages:

### 1. **Source Parsing** (`src/source-parser.ts`)
The CLI accepts multiple source formats and normalizes them:
- **GitHub shorthand**: `owner/repo` → resolves to `https://github.com/owner/repo.git`
- **GitHub with subpath**: `owner/repo/path/to/skill` → extracts subpath via `sanitizeSubpath()`
- **GitHub with skill filter**: `owner/repo@skill-name` → stored as `skillFilter`
- **Full GitHub URLs**: `https://github.com/owner/repo` or tree URLs
- **GitLab**: `gitlab.com/owner/repo` or `gitlab:owner/repo`
- **Git SSH**: `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`
- **Local paths**: Absolute or relative paths like `./my-skills`

Source aliases are resolved (e.g., `coinbase/agentWallet` → `coinbase/agentic-wallet-skills`)

### 2. **Git Cloning & Skill Discovery** (`src/add.ts` → `src/skills.ts`)
Once parsed, the source is cloned (or local path used), then `discoverSkills()` searches for SKILL.md files in specific container directories.

### 3. **User Selection & Installation** (`src/add.ts` → `src/installer.ts`)
Skills are discovered, filtered by name (if using `@skill-name`), then installed to agent-specific directories.

---

## Key Directory Assumptions & Layout

### Container Directories (Searched in Priority Order)

The toolchain searches for `SKILL.md` files in these hardcoded locations within a repository:

**Priority 1 (root & flat layouts):**
- Root directory (if contains `SKILL.md`) — returns immediately unless `--full-depth` is set
- `skills/`
- `skills/.curated/`
- `skills/.experimental/`
- `skills/.system/`

**Priority 2 (agent-specific project skill directories):**
- `.aider-desk/skills/`
- `.agents/skills/`
- `.claude/skills/`
- `.cline/skills/`
- `.codex/skills/`
- `.continue/skills/`
- (and ~40 more agent-specific directories)

**Plugin Manifests (if present):**
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — multi-plugin catalog with local `source` paths
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — single plugin at root

### Skill Discovery Depth

The search algorithm has **two depth levels**:

1. **Depth-1 (flat layout)**: Only direct children of container directories
   - Example: `skills/my-skill/SKILL.md` ✓
   
2. **Depth-2 (catalog layout)**: One extra level for categorization
   - Example: `skills/category/my-skill/SKILL.md` ✓
   - Applied only to known skill containers, not the repo root

If no skills found at depth-1/2, a **recursive fallback** search activates (up to depth 5) that scans all subdirectories (excluding `node_modules`, `.git`, `dist`, `build`, `__pycache__`).

### Installation Directory Structure

**Universal Agents** (share one canonical location):
- Project: `.agents/skills/<skill-name>/`
- Global: `~/.agents/skills/<skill-name>/`

**Agent-Specific (non-universal) Agents**:
- Project: `.{agent}/skills/<skill-name>/` (e.g., `.claude/skills/`, `.cursor/skills/`)
- Global: `~/{agent}/skills/` (varies; some use `~/.config/{agent}/skills/`)

**Eve Subagents** (project-only):
- `agent/subagents/<subagent-name>/skills/<skill-name>/`

### Installation Layout

When installing in **symlink mode** (recommended):
1. Source skill is **copied** to canonical location: `.agents/skills/<skill-name>/`
2. Agent-specific symlink is created: `.{agent}/skills/<skill-name>` → `../.agents/skills/<skill-name>`

When installing in **copy mode** (fallback):
- Skill is copied directly to agent-specific location without a canonical copy

---

## Hardcoded Expectations About Skill Structure

### 1. **SKILL.md Frontmatter**
```yaml
---
name: skill-name                    # Required: lowercase, hyphens allowed
description: What this skill does   # Required: human-readable
metadata:
  internal: false                    # Optional: hide from normal discovery if true
---
```

- **name** and **description** are required fields
- Both must be strings (not numbers or booleans)
- Name is normalized: lowercase, spaces/underscores → hyphens
- Invalid SKILL.md files are skipped with warnings but don't break discovery

### 2. **Security Assumptions**
- **Path traversal protection**: 
  - Subpaths must not contain `..` segments: `sanitizeSubpath()` validates and rejects
  - Skill names are sanitized: `sanitizeName()` removes special chars, limits to 255 chars
  - Both `isPathSafe()` and `isSubpathSafe()` prevent escaping from base directories

- **Symlink safety**:
  - Prevents circular symlinks and self-referential links
  - Uses `realpath()` to resolve through parent directory symlinks
  - Validates that canonical and agent paths don't overlap

### 3. **Subpath Resolution**
When specifying a skill in a subdirectory:
```bash
npx skills add owner/repo/path/to/skill  # Looks for ./path/to/skill/SKILL.md or ./path/to/skill/*/SKILL.md
```

The toolchain searches for `SKILL.md` at:
1. Exact path: `./path/to/skill/SKILL.md`
2. Catalog depth: `./path/to/skill/*/SKILL.md`

### 4. **Plugin Manifest Convention**
If using `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, skill paths must:
- Start with `./` (e.g., `./skills/my-skill`)
- Be relative to `pluginRoot` (default is repo root)
- Not traverse outside base directory

### 5. **Installed Project Skills Tracking**
The toolchain tracks installed skills in:
- `~/.claude/skills-lock.json` (global)
- `.claude/skills-lock.json` (project-level, if exists)

These prevent duplicate installs and track installation source/version.

---

## Key Files Reference

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `src/source-parser.ts` | Parses all source formats (shorthand, URLs, paths) |
| `src/skills.ts` | Core `discoverSkills()` - searches containers for SKILL.md |
| `src/installer.ts` | Handles symlink/copy installation, path safety |
| `src/add.ts` | CLI entry point, orchestrates resolution & installation |
| `src/agents.ts` | Defines agent configs with skill directory paths |
| `src/plugin-manifest.ts` | Plugin manifest parsing & validation |
| `src/constants.ts` | Defines `AGENTS_DIR = '.agents'`, `SKILLS_SUBDIR = 'skills'` |

---

## Summary of Layout Assumptions

1. **Single canonical location per skill** (`.agents/skills/<name>`) shared via symlinks
2. **Agent-specific directories** follow pattern `.{agent}/skills/` or `~/{agent}/skills/`
3. **Skills are discovered only in predefined containers** — no arbitrary directory scanning
4. **Depth-2 catalogs** allow `container/category/skill/SKILL.md` pattern
5. **Plugin manifests** explicitly declare paths using `./` relative convention
6. **All paths are validated** for safety — no `..` allowed, canonicalized checks prevent loops
7. **Name normalization** — spaces/underscores become hyphens, special chars stripped

  internal: false                    # Optional: hide from normal discovery if true
---

- Name is normalized: lowercase, spaces/underscores → hyphens

- **Path traversal protection**:

  - Skill names are sanitized: `sanitizeName()` removes special chars, limits to 255 chars
  - Both `isPathSafe()` and `isSubpathSafe()` prevent escaping from base directories

  - Prevents circular symlinks and self-referential links
  - Uses `realpath()` to resolve through parent directory symlinks
  - Validates that canonical and agent paths don't overlap

### 3. **Subpath Resolution**
When specifying a skill in a subdirectory:
```bash

```

The toolchain searches for `SKILL.md` at:
1. Exact path: `./path/to/skill/SKILL.md`
2. Catalog depth: `./path/to/skill/*/SKILL.md`

If using `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, skill paths must:
- Start with `./` (e.g., `./skills/my-skill`)
- Be relative to `pluginRoot` (default is repo root)
- Not traverse outside base directory

The toolchain tracks installed skills in:
- `~/.claude/skills-lock.json` (global)
- `.claude/skills-lock.json` (project-level, if exists)
